attributes.body_ja:
「ほど」は、だいたいの程度（ていど）や量（りょう）、範囲（はんい）などを表（あらわ）すときに使（つか）われる表現（ひょうげん）です。漢字（かんじ）では「程（ほど）」と書（か）きます。「ほど」は、「これより以上（いじょう）ではない」（または「これより以下（いか）ではない」）のように、限度（げんど）に「達（たっ）している」状態（じょうたい）を表（あらわ）します。「くらい」と似（に）ていますが、「くらい」は話（はな）し手（て）が正確（せいかく）な数（かず）に自信（じしん）がないときに使（つか）われる表現（ひょうげん）で、限度（げんど）を表（あらわ）すニュアンスはありません。

「ほど」は、連体形（れんたいけい）（名詞（めいし）に直接（ちょくせつ）付（つ）けられる形（かたち））の語（ご）に付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。

「くらい」は、ある基準（きじゅん）より上（うえ）でも下（した）でも、そのあたりのだいたいの範囲（はんい）を表（あらわ）すときに使（つか）われます。しかし、「程（ほど）」は限度（げんど）を表（あらわ）すので、それを超（こ）えるときには使（つか）われません。また、「ほど」は、実際（じっさい）の程度（ていど）がそれより小（ちい）さくても、（A）の限度（げんど）を強（つよ）く表（あらわ）すときによく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
ほど, coming from the kanji 程（ほど） 'an extent', is used for describing rough estimates about the 'amount' of something. However, unlike expressions such as くらい (which focuses more on the speaker's uncertainty about the exact number), ほど puts emphasis on the upper (or lower) limit of something as having been 'reached'. Due to this, it is usually translated as 'so much that (A)', or 'to the extent that (A)'.

ほど can be added on to the end of the attributive form of any word. The attributive form being the form that is able to be partnered directly with nouns.

Caution

Although くらい may be used to describe something that is 'around' a certain extent (regardless of whether it is above or below that extent), 程（ほど） refers specifically to the 'limit' of something, and therefore cannot be used to describe something that exceeds the stated limit. Due to this, it is regularly used to express some sort of exaggerated limit of (A), when the real extent is far below that.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: The difference between くらい and ほど in hyperbole
Using 「ほど」 to express the extent of something

attributes.body: ほど (sometimes seen in kanji as 程) has the basic meaning of 'extent'. ほど〜ない is used for comparisons meaning 'not as (A) as (B)', e.g. 彼ほど背が高くない ('I'm not as tall as him.'). When used alone, ほど means 'so much that (A)' or 'to the extent of (A)', e.g. 驚くほど静かだった ('It was quiet to a surprising degree.' or 'It was so quiet that I was surprised.').

first_relatable.meaning: Is not as…as, Isn't... like..., Not to the extent of...

attributes.body: Both くらい and ほど can express extent in the sense of 'so much that (A)' or 'to the extent of (A)', and are often interchangeable, e.g. 驚くくらい静かだった / 驚くほど静かだった ('It was quiet to a surprising degree.') くらい (also written as ぐらい) tends to sound slightly more colloquial, and each word has other uses where they may not be interchangeable.

first_relatable.title: くらい ②
first_relatable.meaning: To the extent that, So…that, About the only thing that...

second_relatable.title: ほど
second_relatable.meaning: The more, About, To the extent that, So much… that

attributes.body: Both relate to expressing extent, but with different emphasis. は～くらいです highlights something as the only or most notable case, like 'about the only (A) is (B)', e.g. できるのは田中さんくらいです ('Mr. Tanaka's about the only person who can do it.') ほど expresses extent or intensity, e.g. 驚くほど静かだった ('It was quiet to a surprising degree.')

attributes.body: まで and ほど both mean 'to the extent of,' but with different uses. まで emphasizes inclusion or a surprising limit, e.g. 骨まで食べた ('He even ate the bones.'). ほど means 'so much that' and often describes degree or intensity, e.g. 痛いほど分かる ('I understand to the point that it hurts.').

attributes.body: くらい (often ぐらい in speech) expresses an approximate degree or extent. It's often used with number + counter expressions (the くらい① form), as in 10分くらいかかった = 'It took about ten minutes.' ほど can be used similarly, but is more formal and carries the nuance of an upper limit—e.g., 10分ほど implies 'about, but no more than ten minutes.'

second_relatable.title: ほど
second_relatable.meaning: The more, About, To the extent that, So much… that

attributes.body: ほど (sometimes written in kanji as 程) has the basic meaning of 'extent'. ば〜ほど shows a proportional relationship, similar to 'the more (A), the more (B)', e.g. 練習すればするほど上手になる ('The more you practice, the better you get.') When used alone, ほど means 'so much that (A)' or 'to the extent of (A)', e.g. 驚くほど静かだった ('It was quiet to a surprising degree.' / 'It was so quiet that I was surprised.')
